stories.excerpt: The president of Paraguay, Pedro Alliana, announced on Tuesday that the recovery of pension funds deposited in Ueno Bank will be a priority for his government. The intervention in the financial institution has put at risk around 800 million dollars (about 716 million euros) belonging to public bodies, including resources from five retirement funds, and has triggered a political crisis that ended with the removal of Santiago Peña from office. Among the institutions affected is the Social Security Institute (IPS), which is responsible for managing pensions and part of the country's health services. Uncertainty over the recovery of these funds has caused growing concern among workers and retirees. Alliana, who took over the presidency last Friday, has pledged to protect citizens' savings and to speed up compensation after the banking collapse. The president has said that around 1.74 million depositors have received payments totalling 330 million dollars through the Deposit Guarantee Fund.

stories.excerpt: Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, is back in federal custody in Florida after allegedly removing his ankle monitor, according to court documents. Markle appeared before a federal magistrate judge in the Florida city of Tampa on Tuesday and was denied bond. Prosecutors say he removed the monitor early that morning. US Judge Lindsay S Griffin found on Tuesday that Markle had violated the conditions of his pretrial release, court documents show. Markle, who has denied possessing images of child sex abuse, was arrested in Florida last week and placed under house detention. He was also ordered to wear a location monitoring device.
